h: Shemittah Makes Divine Ownership Last Beyond the Year of Rest

p: וְשָׁבְתָה הָאָרֶץ שַׁבָּת לַה׳ וְגוֹ׳ (וַיִּקְרָא כה, ב)
"And the land shall rest a Shabbos to Hashem, etc." (Vayikra 25:2).
just as it says of the Shabbos of Creation."
just as with the Shabbos of Creation,
for the sake of the body's rest,
as they said in the Midrash
וְאִם אֵינוֹ נָח יוֹם אֶחָד בַּשָּׁבוּעַ
if he does not rest one day a week,
because the Holy One, blessed is He, commanded
to cease and rest on it,
as they said in the Midrash
just as I rested on it";
that is, for the sake of Hashem
and not for one's own benefit.
So too in the seventh year,
in order to leave the field fallow
so that it give more of its strength
but the resting shall be for the sake of Hashem,
because of the command of the Holy One, blessed is He.
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, already asked:
the intent must be for the sake of Hashem,
with all the festivals "shabbaton" is written,
And this is because the holiness of Shabbos
is fixed and established by Hashem Yisbarach,
and Yisrael do not have the power
for so the nun indicates diminution,
as in the derivation of "ishon" from "ish"
which corresponds to the holiness of Shabbos;
for there are six days among the festivals
and they correspond to the six workdays;
corresponds to the holiness of Shabbos,
for Hashem Yisbarach gave Yisrael the power
to instill the holiness of Shabbos as well.
for Yisrael instill the holiness of Shabbos
which is forbidden in food preparation
in Chiddushei Aggados, beginning of Yoma);
"And you shall count for yourselves from the day after the Shabbos";
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
"And the land shall rest a Shabbos to Hashem, etc."
and this is before the warnings to man;
and afterward the warnings are written:
"a shabbas shabbaton shall be for the land,
and after the warnings it is written,
"a year of rest shall be for the land" (Vayikra 25:5),
"and the Shabbos of the land shall be for you
and they themselves are what is alluded to
in the three holinesses directed upward:
"And the land shall rest a Shabbos to Hashem,"
that the holiness is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
before the Holy One, blessed is He:
and the seventh year among the years, etc.,
before the warnings to man about the labors:
that the land of itself will rest
through its being a Shabbos to Hashem.
and Rashi, of blessed memory, explained:
the level of Yaakov, Zeir Anpin,
and this is "holy for all eternity."
וּבָזֶה כְּתִיב גַּם כֵּן שַׁבָּת לַה׳
And in this too "a Shabbos to Hashem" is written,
for this too is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach:
for the two holinesses of Shabbos
are from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
and here it counts from above to below.
"a year of rest shall be for the land";
and here it does not say "a Shabbos to Hashem,"
and it is after all the warnings to man;
namely the holiness that is from the side of man.
And at the end of all:
"And the Shabbos of the land shall be for you to eat";
who noted that the Shabbos is not eaten;
that the fruits of the seventh year
will have holiness instilled in them
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
for the fruits of the seventh year
as they said in the Gemara,
"he eats it with the holiness of the seventh year";
and they learned from the language of the pasuk,
that redemption does not take effect on them,
and that it takes hold of their monetary value
in the heart of the eater too.
And the seventh year resembles Shabbos,
and it is called first just "Shabbos,"
for the beginning of the holiness, from Atika,
which is in the heights above,
so that the holiness be fixed in the heart
for the essence of the mitzvah of the seventh year
that everything belongs to Hashem Yisbarach;
as it says afterward regarding Yovel,
for you are strangers and residents, etc." (Vayikra 25:23);
and if yours is not Mine,
it is enough for the servant to be like his master."
That is: if you keep the mitzvah of the seventh year
and recognize that yours is Mine,
and I will give you the land;
and if yours is not Mine,
and you do not keep the seventh year,
then it is enough for the servant to be like his master:
"and you are strangers and residents with Me"
I and you will go into exile,
"Then the land shall be appeased for its Shabbosos";
and because of this was the exile of Bavel.
And although this is said regarding Yovel,
from the pasuk "for it is holy,"
that is, the seventh year and Yovel
And in the seventh year itself,
he recognizes that the land is Hashem's;
and for this to be fixed in his heart
when he returns to working the land,
so that he not forget afterward
for through the union of the two holinesses
it becomes fixed in the heart.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר עַל הָאַזְהָרוֹת לָאָדָם
And afterward it speaks of the warnings to man,
for which reason it is called "shabbaton"
and about this it says afterward,
in the heart of the eater,
